description: Maryland-only rules checked against the Transportation Article and Courts Article. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: On divided highways in a Maryland residential district, the statutory maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 21-801.1(b)(3) sets 35 mph on divided highways in a residential district. Undivided residential highways stay at 30.

questions.q: Outside the business and residential districts named in the statute, Maryland's maximum is 50 mph on undivided highways and
questions.explanation: Section 21-801.1(b)(4) and (b)(5) set 50 mph on undivided highways in other locations and 55 mph on divided highways in other locations. A limit over 55 may be established only on an interstate or expressway, and no limit over 70 may be established.

questions.q: Maryland forbids establishing or continuing a maximum speed over 55 mph on a highway that is
options: Not an interstate highway or an expressway
A divided highway in a residential district
questions.explanation: Section 21-801.1(e)(1) says a maximum of more than 55 mph may not be established or continued on any highway that is not an interstate or an expressway. Paragraph (2) adds that more than 70 mph may not be established on any highway.

questions.q: In a Maryland school zone where a school crossing guard is posted to help students cross, during the hours posted on the school-zone signs, the maximum speed limit
options: Is 20 mph whether or not a guard is posted
Is 25 mph only in Baltimore City
questions.explanation: Section 21-803.1(f) says the maximum speed limit may not exceed 35 mph in that school zone during the hours posted on the signs. A school-zone limit established under the section is in effect when posted on appropriate signs. The section does not set one number for every school zone.

questions.q: Maryland defines 'under the influence of alcohol per se' as an alcohol concentration at the time of testing of
questions.explanation: Transportation §11-174.1(a) uses 0.08 or more by those two measures. Driving or attempting to drive while under the influence of alcohol per se is prohibited by §21-902(a). 0.08 or more, measured by grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood or per 210 liters of breath.

questions.q: An alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more at the time of testing is prima facie evidence that the person
options: Was under the influence of alcohol per se
Was driving while impaired by alcohol, which the code instead ties to 0.07 but less than 0.08
Was driving with alcohol in the person's blood, and was driving in violation of an alcohol restriction under §16-113
Cannot be prosecuted unless the result also reaches 0.08
questions.explanation: Courts Article §10-307(e) and (f) make 0.02 or more prima facie evidence of driving with alcohol in the blood and of violating an alcohol restriction under Transportation §16-113. Subsection (g) reserves the per se under-the-influence rule for 0.08 or more.

questions.q: For points accumulated within any two-year period, the Maryland MVA shall suspend the license at
options: 12 points, which is a revocation rather than the first suspension
questions.explanation: Transportation §16-404(a) sends a warning letter at 3 points, requires a driver-improvement program at 5 points, suspends at 8 points, and revokes at 12 points, with the exceptions stated in §16-405.

questions.q: Except for the longer alcohol-related periods in the same subsection, an initial Maryland suspension for accumulating points is
options: Not less than 2 days and not more than 30 days
Not less than 15 days and not more than 90 days
questions.explanation: Section 16-404(c)(1) sets an initial suspension at not less than 2 days nor more than 30 days. A subsequent suspension is not less than 15 days nor more than 90 days, subject to the longer alcohol-related periods in that subsection.

questions.q: The MVA may not issue a learner's instructional permit to a person who has not reached
questions.explanation: Transportation §16-103 says the Administration may not issue a learner's instructional permit before age 15 years and 9 months, a provisional license before 16 years and 6 months, or a license before 18.

questions.q: An applicant under 19 generally may not take the provisional-license skills or road exam until 9 months after receiving the learner's permit and until the applicant has at least
options: 40 hours of practice, including 10 at night
50 hours of practice, including 10 at night
60 hours of practice, including 10 at night
questions.explanation: Section 16-105 requires the 9-month wait and, unless an exception in that subsection applies, an approved driver-education course of at least 30 classroom hours and 6 highway hours, plus at least 60 hours of supervised practice. Ten of those practice hours must occur from 30 minutes before sunset until 30 minutes after sunrise. The supervisor must be at least 21 and licensed for at least 3 years. 60 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, 10 hours of which fall in the stated sunset-to-sunrise period.

questions.q: A provisional licensee under 18 may drive unsupervised only
options: From 5 a.m. to midnight, with exceptions
At any hour after the first 30 days
questions.explanation: Section 16-113(d) limits unsupervised driving to 5 a.m. through midnight. Between midnight and 5 a.m. the licensee must be supervised by a licensed driver at least 21, or be driving for employment, a school class or official school activity, an organized volunteer program, or an athletic event or related training. The hour restriction expires at 18.

questions.q: In Maryland, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Maryland issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years and 9 months at the earliest.

provenance.manual: Learner's Permit | MDOT Motor Vehicle Administration

questions.q: In Maryland, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Maryland requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 9 months.

provenance.manual: Maryland Driver's Manual - Motor Vehicle Administration

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Maryland complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Maryland requires 60 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Maryland teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Maryland requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

provenance.manual: Maryland Driver's Manual - Motor Vehicle Administration

questions.q: In Maryland, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Maryland, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16½ years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Maryland not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Maryland restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

provenance.manual: Maryland Driver's Manual - Motor Vehicle Administration

questions.q: In Maryland, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Maryland drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Maryland car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Maryland car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Maryland car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 88% to pass the Maryland car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Prepare for a Driver's License Test \| MVA

questions.q: In Maryland, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Maryland, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

provenance.manual: Maryland Driver's Manual - Motor Vehicle Administration

questions.q: In Maryland, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Maryland sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Maryland, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Maryland brings a suspension of 270 days.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Maryland residential district?
questions.explanation: Maryland sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Maryland?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Maryland can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Maryland's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Maryland: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Maryland?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Maryland, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

provenance.manual: Maryland Driver's Manual - Motor Vehicle Administration

questions.q: How is Maryland's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Maryland seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Maryland?
questions.explanation: Maryland requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Maryland's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Maryland requires at least $30,000 / $60,000 / $15,000.

questions.q: Under Maryland's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Maryland can suspend an adult's license at 8 points in 24 months.
